question: Why does the doctrine of difference fail to establish real spatial distinction?
premises: If space itself is taken as the common place, everything would collapse into one place.
If difference is explained by limiting conditions, those conditions still require spatial distinction.
The distinction of limiting conditions would itself depend on further distinction.
inference: In a doctrine of difference, spatial distinction cannot be grounded without circular dependence on limiting conditions.
plain_english: In the doctrine of difference, if space is the common place, everything would be in one place; but if difference comes from limiting conditions, even those differently placed conditions depend on further difference.
